newsitem.title: UK: London golds fixes off floor but support tentative.
newsitem.headline: London golds fixes off floor but support tentative.

text.p: Gold slipped to its lowest fixing since March 24, 1993 during London's Wednesday morning, although it managed to edge slightly up from the lows by the afternoon setting.
Fears of central bank selling, lack of investor interest and sales by producers who are seeking to protect profits against even lower prices have flattened the gold market this week.
Gold was fixed at $332.15 per ounce at 1400 GMT, up from $331.45 in the morning but still under Tuesday's $333.70.

Dealers said light short covering after the market found some support at the low helped prices stabilise, and analysts said further plunges might be postponed until after the U.S. Independence Day holiday this weekend.
New York Comex August gold futures price was at $333.40 down $1.70 at the fixing having gapped lower to $332.30 in response to weaker bullion on the opening.
The market also awaited any pointers to changes in U.S. interest rate policy after a Federal Open Market Committee meeting later Wednesday.

"Short term there is scope for a covering bounce," one analyst said, but he also noted that investment funds had increased short positions over the past couple of weeks. It would take more than revitalised physical demand to counterbalance that, he added.
Physical demand has been notably lower this week despite weaker prices, partly because Hong Kong has been closed since Monday while the territory reverts to Chinese rule.

One analyst said a developing El Nino warm ocean current might have an impact on the gold market if, as has happened before, it results in a poor Indian monsoon. Bad rains may hit harvests, crimp farm incomes and reduce demand for gold in rural India.

"There are signs of a major El Nino effect which could bring India its first poor monsoon in seven years," the analyst said. "The strength of the agricultural sector has driven the boom in demand for gold in India."
A critical level was $330.00 beneath which psychologically driven sales could probe the 1993 low of $326.10, analysts said.
Silver was relatively untouched by gold's moves and was unchanged at $4.66/$4.68 at the gold fixing.
Platinum and palladium have broken decisively with gold but both were near intraday lows after news that major supplier Russia would open its delayed 1997 expoprt programme on July 10.
Platinum was down $17.50 at $423.00/$426.00 and palladium down $4.00 at $190.00/$193.00. --Brian Spoors +44 171 542 8058
